summary: Approved the treasurer's report, payment of bills, and fund transfers.
First reading of a revision to the animal-control ordinance (06-0321-A) adding a trap-neuter-vaccinate-return program for community cats.
Adopted Resolution 26-0422-A executing the County Road Aid agreement with the state Transportation Cabinet.
Awarded FY2026-27 road-material and service bids (aggregate, asphalt, fuel, paving and more); rejected the red-gravel bids for resubmission.
Awarded fire-extinguisher service to Fire Safe Services and county-facility pest control to McGee Pest Control (about $667/year savings).
Approved an amended 2026 budget (no change to the bottom line) and a CD renewal at The Murray Bank.
Approved a 4-year, $365,000 loan at 4.53% (FNB Bank) to purchase two dump trucks.
Approved the financial statement, bills, and cash transfers.
Second reading and adoption of Ordinance 20-0320-A, a budget amendment involving Sheriff's funds.
Approved the County Clerk's 2025 final settlement.
Adopted Resolution 26-0320-C (agreement with the state Transportation Cabinet) for replacement of the Howard Road bridge, funded through CCBIP at $800,000.
Adopted Resolution 26-0320-D supporting a grant application (up to about $1 million) toward a new fire station, and 26-0320-E supporting agricultural hemp development.
Made board appointments to the Industrial Development Authority and the hospital (MCCH) board; approved revised job descriptions.
Approved the financial report and payment of bills; approved 2026 incentive pay for several officials.
Approved the Sheriff's 2025 excess-fee final settlement and agreed to return $202,189.26 to the Sheriff's office, disbursed quarterly (March-June), with a related budget-amendment first reading.

Adopted Resolution 26-0218-A (adopting Sack Farm Drive for 911 addressing), 26-0218-B (authorizing application for KY Homeland Security grants), and 26-0218-C (supporting HB 557, cited as benefiting the jail budget).
Reappointed members to the Ethics Board.
Held the Grubbs Road bridge bids until the next meeting to standardize a 20-foot width.
Entered executive session under KRS 61.810(1)(f); returned with no action taken.
Approved the treasurer's report, bills, and cash transfers; approved a contract with ACA Prime for 1095 health-insurance forms.
Adopted resolutions honoring a retiring jail deputy (26-0121-A), memorializing the late Magistrate Johnny Gingles (26-0121-B), and joining the America250KY Liberty Tree planting (26-0121-C).
Made board appointments to the Hazel 641 Water District.
Approved a contract with Shelter Planners of America for a first-step survey toward a new animal shelter.

Discussed a joint Community Development Block Grant application with the City of Murray to renovate the Senior Citizens Center; the Judge-Executive disclosed a conflict of interest and said he would abstain on that matter.
Approved the financial statement, bills, and budget/cash transfers.
Approved the 2026 County Clerk budget and salary order and set election-worker pay at $250.
Approved the 2026 holiday and meeting schedule.

Adopted resolutions recognizing local students and the Murray High football team; discontinuing county maintenance on Nova Lane (after a public hearing with no comment); supporting an MCIDA training-center grant application (25-1217-D); and a Transportation Cabinet agreement for the Potts Road bridge using CCBIP funds (25-1217-E).
Renewed the EMS affiliation agreement with Calloway County Fire-Rescue and approved the surplus of two Sheriff's vehicles.
Approved the financial statement, bills, and transfers.
Approved the 2026 Sheriff's budget and the annual order setting maximum Sheriff's-office salaries at $2,200,000.
Adopted Resolution 25-1119-A for a CCBIP agreement with the Transportation Cabinet to repair/replace the Graham Road bridge (state-managed work).
Created a county Cemetery Board (five members) and reappointed/appointed UK Cooperative Extension board members.
Awarded the Doores Trail culvert-to-bridge project to Youngblood at $415,389 (FEMA-submitted).
Approved the financial statement.
Approved jail firearms-policy updates.
Authorized a Regional Development Agency Assistance Program application of $153,846 toward a Workforce Training Center, and signed an Emergency Management Performance Grant.
Authorized a FEMA-grant culvert replacement on Doores Trail (county share is a portion of a statewide allocation).
Approved changing the county cellular provider from Verizon to T-Mobile, and authorized an interlocal agreement with the City of Murray for the Weaks Senior Citizens Center grant.
Approved the financial statement, bills, and transfers.
Second reading and adoption of Ordinance 25-0924-A regulating medical-cannabis business operations (public hearing, no comment).
Adopted a resolution discontinuing road maintenance on Eldridge Lane and began the removal process for Nova Lane and East Y Road.
Made appointments to the Tourism Commission, Dexter-Almo Water District, 911 Appeals Board, and Library Board.
Authorized listing the remaining five county-owned lots in Western Shores; authorized Road Department fall maintenance on the Hwy 641 lot (per Resolution 24-0717-A requiring full-Court consent).
Approved the financial statement, bills, and cash transfers.
Second reading and adoption of Ordinance 25-0821-A setting the 2025 county tax rates (public hearing, no comment).
First reading of an ordinance regulating medical-cannabis operations.
Heard special taxing-district rates (Library 4.8c real property; Extension 2.5c, up from 1.5c, citing reserve drawdown).
Adopted resolutions accepting Victory Lane into the county road system (25-0820-E), accepting 2025 FLEX funds (25-0820-D), and supporting a DRA grant for Hopkins Road (25-0820-C).
Entered executive session under KRS 61.810(1)(f) and (1)(b).
Approved the financial statement, bills, transfers, and a $100,000 transfer to the Road Department.
First reading of the 2025 county tax rate at 14.10 cents/$100 — described as 4% over the compensating rate, an estimated ~$29,000 in added revenue (rate last increased in 2021).
Adopted the EM State Mutual Aid agreement and resolution 25-0716-A.
Awarded a $73,600 contract to Henry and Son to paint the courthouse; approved an HVAC replacement (Thornton's) for the EM office.
Approved an updated drug-testing contract (Tri-State), with a rebid to follow per the two-year requirement.
vote_notes: Street-Legal Special Purpose Vehicle ordinance 25-0716-A (second reading): passed 4-1 — Squire Cherry voted no; Judge Imes and Squires Rister, Crutcher, Stewart voted aye.

summary: Approved a $529.22 budget transfer to the County Attorney salary line.
Authorized a $300,000 transfer (money market to general to jail) to cover July jail insurance and workers'-comp bills.
Adopted a resolution for a Transportation Cabinet agreement to repair/replace the Charley Miller Road bridge with grant funds up to $490,000.
Discussed (no action) a ~$1.8M CCBIP award (7.3% of the first $25M round) for four bridges, and an $51,805 KYTC 80/20 swap from Grubbs Road to Cook Store bridge (about $6,000 added from road funds).
Approved the financial statement, bills, transfers, and the second reading of budget amendment 25-0618-A (Flex Funds).
Set the Health Department tax rates for 2026 (unchanged).
Approved the Sheriff's 2024 tax settlement.
Adopted Resolution 25-0618-A (administrative-code amendments) and 25-0618-B (supporting the Job Corps program).
Approved a 2.9% cost-of-living increase for non-elected county employees and appointed Chris Franklin as Road Supervisor (KRS 179.020).
Discontinued Sharmae Lane and adjusted John Purdom/Harry Truman drive names.
Approved the financial report, bills, transfers, and first reading of a Flex-funds budget amendment.
Second reading and adoption of the 2025-2026 county budget (public hearing, no comment).
Adopted Resolution 25-0521-A (Transportation Cabinet agreement) for replacement of the Clayton Town Road bridge.
Approved a $89,629 Grubbs Road bridge repair contract (Jim Smith Contracting) and a 4-year paving agreement for 3.58 miles in Western Shores.
Authorized a purchase order for two dump trucks (~$174,000 each, delivery in 2026) and a $1,500 TVA 26A permit application for the Boatwright Trail project.
Special session on the disposition of the old Old Salem Road bridge after the new bridge's completion.
Approved, by general consensus (all ayes), keeping the historic structure for community use as a small fishing/nature area, with KACO consulted on liability and Fish & Wildlife on collaboration.

Authorized a $1,500,000 12-month CD at The Murray Bank (4.25% APY) funded from the jail-grant account, and a $625,000 12-month CD (4.25% APY) funded from the E911 account, with matching budget line items added.
Approved issuing an RFP (two-week timeline) for the Grubbs Road bridge, weighing closure against an estimated $91,000 repair.
Discussed (no action) the 2026-2027 County Priority Project Program.
Approved the financial report, bills, second reading of a budget amendment (Sheriff excess fees and the 80/20 bridge program), the annual standing order, and a cash-transfer blanket order.
Accepted reduced LGEA funds ($8,000 down to $6,000) and noted a MAG block-grant payment of $163,980 (third payment).
Adopted Resolution 25-0416-A for the County Road Aid Cooperative Program ($1,649,680.39 for FY beginning July 1, 2025).
First reading of the 2025-2026 county budget totaling $20,277,141.58.
First reading of the street-legal special-purpose-vehicle ordinance (SB 63 opt-in); reauthorized standing committees and added a Long Range Planning & Financing committee.
Adopted Resolution 25-0324-A for a Rural Secondary Program agreement with the Transportation Cabinet to address drainage at the Dodd Road bridge.
Entered and exited executive session under KRS 61.810(1)(f) with no action taken.
Approved the financial report, bills, transfers, and a first-reading budget amendment (Sheriff excess fees and 80/20 bridge funds).
Noted a $157,227 MAG block-grant payment (second payment) to Clark Construction.
Approved the County Clerk's 2024 final settlement and recurring 911 software contracts (Active911, Virtual Academy).
Adopted a PADD/Murray Art Guild CDBG administration resolution (25-0319-E) and resolutions honoring community members.
Noted the jail budget's $430,000 personnel-line increase tied to the salary survey.
Approved the financial report and bills, including a $83,862 MAG block-grant payment to Clark Construction.
Approved the Sheriff's 2024 final settlement ($259,727.37 turned over) and returned the funds for deputy salaries in four payments.
Adopted resolutions for Transportation Cabinet agreements on the Clayton Road bridge ($430,000) and Furches Trail bridge ($505,000), and a Homeland Security application (24-0219-E).
Confirmed a $1,786,301 25% local match (G.R.A.N.T./HB 9) tied to a WK&T USDA ReConnect award for ~94 miles of fiber.
Approved the lowest Taylor Store bridge bid ($143,626, Jim Smith Construction) and up to $35,000 for Almo bridge repairs.
Approved the financial statement, bills, and a transfer.
Approved 911 policy changes and the annual Calloway County Fire-Rescue affiliation.
Heard 2024 jail and sheriff reports; noted research on 1,506 unpaid 2023 property-tax bills and related legislation (KRS 132.012).
Entered executive session under KRS 61.810(1)(b) on personnel matters; returned with no action.
Approved the financial statement, bills, transfers, and a $180,062.50 check (on delivery) for a Road Department dump truck.
Approved Sheriff and Clerk administrative-code changes and the 2025 County Clerk budget and salary order.
Approved the 2025 holiday/meeting schedule (12 observed holidays).

Adopted Resolution 24-1218-A (revised administrative code, part-time holiday pay), 24-1218-B (remaining ARPA funds for the Old Salem Road bridge), and 24-1218-C (designating MCIDA to receive TVA funds).
Noted 2024 auto-insurance-premium-tax use: $1.1M for paving and $700K allocated for bridges; authorized TVA permit applications for Boatwright Landing and Chandler Park.
vote_notes: Grounds-maintenance contract (Swift Environmental): passed 4-1 — Judge Imes voted no.
Tourism Commission appointments: Squire Rister abstained (board member).

summary: Approved the financial statement, bills, and cash transfers.
Amended the Sheriff's 2024 budget (reflecting returned excess fees) and approved jail-policy updates.
Second reading and adoption of amendments to the Solar Farm ordinance 24-0417-A (public hearing, no comment).
Adopted Resolution 24-1016-A for the 80/20 KYTC bridge program (up to $80,000 reimbursement toward a $100,000+ five-bridge project) and 24-1016-C naming two private drives for 911.
Approved 911 purchases: a Nelson Systems maintenance renewal ($13,627.53) and three solar battery-backup systems for radio towers ($17,160).
Approved the financial statement, bills, and transfers.
Held a public hearing and adopted the 2024-25 tax rate at $0.14/$100.
First reading of an amendment to the Solar Farm ordinance 24-0417-A (floating systems, TVA/PSC rules, fees).
Approved an ER Assist contract for FEMA debris-removal coordination after the May storm (with a local-hire provision).
Adopted Resolution 24-0918-A (drug- and alcohol-free workplace policy) and 24-0918-B (new job descriptions); dismissed the 911 Relocation Committee (no relocation).
vote_notes: 2024-25 county tax rate ($0.14 per $100): passed 4-1 — Squire Crutcher voted no; Judge Imes and Squires Rister, Cherry, Stewart voted aye.

summary: Approved the financial statement, bills, transfers, and the 2023-2024 Treasurer's settlement.
Approved the Sheriff's 2023 tax settlement.
Placed a medical-cannabis question on the 2024 ballot by resolution (see vote note).
Approved the jail's purchase of a 2017 minivan for inmate transport ($5,000); noted a $4,396 jail taser grant.
vote_notes: Resolution 24-0717-A (no action on the 641 & 80 property without full-Court approval at an open meeting): passed with Judge Imes abstaining (four ayes).

Cannabis-referendum resolution for the 2024 ballot (as amended): roll-call passed 3-2 — Squires Stewart, Crutcher, Cherry aye; Squire Rister and Judge Imes nay. (The amendment adding the ballot wording passed unanimously first.)

summary: Adopted Resolution 24-0628-A approving the revised Calloway County Administrative Code.
Adopted Resolution 24-0628-B authorizing transfer of Nelom Brown Drive to the National Park Service.
Approved a budget transfer and authorized payment from LAFTA funds for an Animal Shelter vehicle.
Held discussion (no vote) on the draft medical-cannabis ordinance ahead of the state opening dispensary applications July 1.
Approved the financial statements, bills, cash and budget transfers, and additional payments to Jim Smith Contracting and Murray Paving.
First reading of a 2023-2024 budget amendment for KYTC emergency funds (Coleman Branch and Squire Holland bridges).
Created a new Auto Insurance Tax line item and opened a dedicated Murray Bank account, transferring $942,317.37 from the Road Fund into it.
Adopted Resolution 24-0515-A (County Road Aid Cooperative Program agreement).
Second reading and adoption of the 2024-2025 county budget; first readings of road-acceptance-requirements and medical-cannabis ordinances; accepted Westhaven Lane into the county road system.
vote_notes: Medical-cannabis ballot-question resolution: a motion was made but received no second; it was laid on the clerk's desk with no vote taken.

summary: Approved the financial statements, bills, cash transfers, and the second reading of a budget amendment (public hearing, no comment).
Approved the annual standing order and a blanket cash-transfer order for FY2024-25.
First reading of the FY2024-2025 county budget.
Second reading and adoption of the Solar Farm ordinance 24-0417-A (public hearing; supportive comment from KY Farm Bureau).
Adopted Resolution 24-0417-A (discontinuing Ft. Heiman Road and Nelom Brown Drive) and 24-0417-B (Public Safety Telecommunications Week).
Approved the financial statements, bills, cash transfers, budget transfers, and a first-reading budget amendment.
Approved the County Clerk's 2023 final settlement ($179,475).
First reading of a solar-energy-system licensing ordinance (public hearing/second reading set for April).
Began the KRS process to remove Ft. Heiman Road and Nelom Brown Road from county maintenance (pending National Park Service deed transfer).
Split the county pest-control contract between Bug Master and McGee; adopted Homeland Security (24-0320-A) and road/PADD/CDBG resolutions (24-0320-B through -G).
Approved the financial statements and bills.
Approved the Sheriff's final settlement ($242,673.22 in excess fees turned over) and returned the funds for deputy support over four months (March-June).
Approved a Regional Mutual Aid Agreement and accepted Hill Drive and Landon Lane into the county road system.
Discontinued a portion of Mills Trail after a public-comment period (deemed to serve no public purpose by two viewers and the Road Supervisor).
Reappointed two members to the Weaks Center Board.
Approved the financial statements and payment of bills.
Authorized moving forward on Coleman Branch and Squire Holland bridge repairs (Jim Smith Contracting), pending an 80/20 state grant match.
Heard 2023 jail and sheriff reports.

Adopted Resolution 24-0124-A (accepting Edinborough Drive West and Starview Trail into the county road system), 24-0124-B (Regional Transportation Safety Action Plan), and 24-0124-C (honoring an Eagle Scout).
Appointed a Fiscal Court member to the hospital Personnel Committee and named EM volunteer deputy directors by executive order.

regular_schedule: Third Wednesday of each month at 9:00 a.m., Calloway County Courthouse
